correctness.rationale: For ord_p(q)=13, subgroup has odd order, so no 1- or 2-term vanishing. Each t-summand zero is some primitive 13th root of Phi13 shared with positive coefficient polynomial P_E. Since p≡1 mod13, Phi13 splits squarefree, so p divides cyclotomic resultant iff an admissible primitive root zero exists; choosing another subgroup generator merely permutes primitive roots. Independently enumerated all C(15,3)=455 and C(16,4)=1820 exponent multisets under affine group AGL(1,13), yielding exactly five and sixteen disjoint orbits; computed all 21 absolute norms via symbolic SymPy cyclotomic resultants (different method than source Bareiss 12x12 determinant), factored exactly. Candidate p for k3 are {53,2731}; for k4 {53,79,131,157,1327,2003,7229,398581}; removing already k3 gives claimed minimum=4 primes. Thus unlisted admissible primes have m≥5, not an asserted exact value.

value.rationale: A complete exact finite-exception classification for a natural arithmetic invariant over all admissible primes at a fixed small multiplicative order, not bounded prime testing. The previously unresolved exceptional prime list and exact 21-orbit certificate are independently useful when studying short additive relations in cyclic multiplicative subgroups. This is a meaningful natural cutoff rather than an arbitrary sample.

limitations: Classifies exactly minima ≤4 at order13 with repetitions and prime moduli, not m values ≥5 or composite moduli.
Resultant certificates are exhaustive over short exponent multisets, not trial division over primes.
